articles.title: Gukesh, Praggnanandhaa get Rs 15 lakh each as Tamil Nadu awards Rs 60 lakh to Chess Olympiad medallists
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay honoured the state's chess players for their performances at the 2026 Chess Olympiad, awarding a total
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay honoured the state's chess players for their performances at the 2026 Chess Olympiad, awarding a total of Rs 60 lakh to five recipients at a ceremony in Chennai on Thursday.World champion D Gukesh and R Praggnanandhaa received Rs 15 lakh each, while Savitha Shri B, R Vaishali and Indian Open team captain Srinath Narayanan were awarded Rs 10 lakh each.Gukesh, Praggnanandhaa among top awardeesGukesh won an individual silver medal and helped India secure silver in the Open team event. His parents, Rajinikanth and Padma, collected the award on his behalf.Praggnanandhaa received the same amount after winning an individual bronze medal on Board 1 and contributing to India's team silver.Savitha Shri earned Rs 10 lakh for her individual gold medal and her role in India's bronze medal-winning women's team. Vaishali, who was also part of the women's team, received Rs 10 lakh. Her father, Rameshbabu, and Praggnanandhaa collected the award on her behalf.Srinath, who captained India's Open team, also received Rs 10 lakh.India finished the Olympiad in Samarkand with silver in the Open section and bronze in the women's competition.Tamil Nadu launches athlete support schemeThe ceremony also recognised medal winners from the Asian Games in Nagoya. According to news agency PTI, the Chief Minister distributed a total of Rs 6.9 crore in incentives to the state's Asian Games and Chess Olympiad medallists.Tamil Nadu also launched its Dream Olympics 2036 scheme, which will provide financial assistance to athletes competing at major events, including the Asian Games, Commonwealth Games and their para-sport equivalents.Selected athletes will receive Rs 50 lakh annually, including a monthly stipend of Rs 1 lakh, to help cover training, nutrition and international competition expenses.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 🚨 Official: Cristiano Ronaldo, suspended by the Portuguese FA
articles.summary: This Saturday at noon, the Portuguese Football Federation officially broke its silence on the psychodrama surrounding Cristiano Ronaldo.In a statement publis...
articles.body:
This Saturday at noon, the Portuguese Football Federation officially broke its silence on the psychodrama surrounding Cristiano Ronaldo .

In a statement published by A Bola, the FPF confirmed the Portuguese legend's provisional suspension.

Disciplinary proceedings have also been opened against him, and the length of his suspension must now be determined.

It is worth recalling that Cristiano Ronaldo admitted in his lengthy statement published on Wednesday night that he should be sanctioned for leaving the Portuguese national team's training camp without permission.

Disciplinary proceedings have been opened against Cristiano Ronaldo dos Santos Aveiro, by decision of the Non-Professional Section dated October 9, 2026, to assess the possible disciplinary implications of the incidents reported on October 7, 2026. Without prejudice to the automatic provisional suspension to which he was subject until the date the proceedings were opened, a non-automatic provisional suspension has been imposed on him, with the urgency of the proceedings acknowledged. The case was referred to the FPF's Disciplinary Investigation Committee on October 10, 2026, and all publicity is prohibited until the investigation is concluded .

In your opinion, how long should Cristiano Ronaldo be suspended?

articles.title: Genoa vs Fiorentina: Lineups and how to watch
articles.summary: The Viola remain as unpredictable as ever as they emerge from the break.
articles.body:
Daniele de Rossi picks Hamed Junior Traoré (Fiorentina beffata) in central midfield and the creaky duo of Stephan El Shaarawy and Junior Messias in attack. Paolo Vanoli springs several surprises. Víctor Valdepeñas returns at leftback but the real news is farther forward. For the first time this season, Nicolò Fagioli and Christ Inao Oulaï will share the pitch. Franco Mastantuono also starts despite rumors he'd be on the bench; he's joined by Wilfried Gnonto and Beto up front.

articles.title: FSU football let one big play become a full-blown disaster vs Louisville
articles.summary: Isaac Brown and Louisville's run game thrashed Florida State football's defense, leaving Mike Norvell befuddled.
articles.body:
Stood in the shadow of his own endzone and down 14-0 in the second quarter, Louisville's Isaac Brown took a handoff, jolted left, and zipped past Florida State's defense down the sideline at L&N Federal Credit Union Stadium for a 97-yard touchdown run.

The play altered the course of the game and sparked a remarkable Louisville turnaround, which resulted in a 44-20 blowout of the Seminoles on Friday, Oct. 9. The loss extended the program's winless streak away from Doak Campbell Stadium to at least 1,057 days.

After Brown's lengthy touchdown run, Louisville recorded 382 rushing yards and rattled off 35 unanswered points and outscored FSU, 44-6. The Cardinals star back recorded 235 rushing yards and had 313 all-purpose yards after he took the opening kickoff of the second half back 71 yards.

"Isaac was a great player tonight. He's a great player; he really took over the game with the kickoff return and then the big runs that he had," a visibly frustrated FSU head coach Mike Norvell told reporters post-game. "But we can't help great players by not doing and being where we need to be."

Louisville reached the 401 rushing yard mark and finished the game with 397 yards after quarterback Lincoln Kienholz knelt three times in victory formation. It saved the Seminoles (3-3, 1-2 ACC) from officially tying for the most rushing yards allowed in a single game, which remains the 401 allowed against Georgia Tech in 2009, but it in no way lessened the embarrassment.

Of the 397 yards, the most allowed under Norvell and second most in program history, 209 came on three scoring plays: Brown's runs of 97 (a Louisville record) and 68 yards, and a 44-yard score from Braxton Jennings. While the Seminoles' defense has been inconsistent this season, its run defense had been a strength in prior games and had mostly limited explosive plays.

Mike Norvell sounds off after FSU's poor defensive game

Entering the game, FSU allowed an average of 119.2 rushing yards per game, ranked 44th in the country, and was fresh off a dominant display against Virginia, where the defense allowed 37 yards . Despite that, the Cardinals tormented the unit, and it left Norvell befuddled.

"It sucked...," Norvell remarked about his defense while thumping a press conference table. "We gave like 20 freaking yards of rushing a week ago, and this week it was 400 yards.

"It's not because, 'Oh hey, we just forgot to coach this week.' You got to go and be able to execute in the moment. You got to be able to take what you do during the course of the week, yeah, short week and all the things, but that's what we coach and work to play for."

Norvell's blunt characterization of the performance is accurate, and the primary culprit of his frustration was Brown.

With fellow Louisville backfield star Keyjuan Brown out with an injury, Issac Brown had 17 carries and averaged 13.8 per attempt. His two rushing scores of 68+ yards make him one of five active players in FBS to have done that in a single game, according to Opta Stats.

And he breathed life into a Louisville team that looked outmatched in the first quarter.

FSU quickly jumped out to a 14-0 lead, with Ashton Daniels setting a program record for most rushing touchdowns by a quarterback with his 10th of the season. Micahi Danzy added a spectacular one-handed grab for the second score, but fate changed on a fourth-and-goal early in the second quarter.

Daniels screen pass to wide receiver Jasen Lopez was blown up and resulted in a turnover on downs. On the next play from scrimmage, Kienholz handed the ball off to Brown, who blazed past the defense for the 97-yard score.

The touchdown led to Louisville's rout of FSU. It also meant the Seminoles surrendered a double-digit lead and ultimately lost by double digits for the second time this season. The other? The 50-36 loss to Alabama.

"What we saw tonight was not good enough," Norvell said. "It was not good enough coaching, not good enough playing. Not good enough."

Norvell and the Seminoles next head to Miami for a rivalry showdown on Saturday, Oct. 17, before a bye week.

Liam Rooney covers Florida State athletics for the Tallahassee Democrat. Contact him via email at LRooney@gannett.com or on Twitter @__liamrooney .
